messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Changing population type
parts:
Could you say more about what you mean by "inbred backcross population"?

read.cross looks to see if the genotypes are all like AA:AB (interpreted as backcross) or AA:AB:BB (interpreted as intercross).

karl



On Mar 12, 2013, at 4:57 PM, Beth <beth....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi there,
>
> I'm pretty brand new to Rqtl and I am trying to create a linkage map for an IBL (inbred backcross population) of 75 individuals. When R reads my map, I get the following output:
>
> --Read the following data:
> 75 individuals
> 630 markers
> 1 phenotypes
> --Estimating genetic map
> --Cross type: f2
>
>
> Is there a way to specify what kind of population is being used? I've seen lots about switching from a bc to a ril but how can I specify that it is a backcross?
>
> I tried the following as well that I found here on the message board but it still gave me the f2 cross type:
>
>> MxEmap <- read.cross("csv","C:/Users/Beth/Documents/Mapping/SNPGenotyping", "MxEmap.csv", class(MxEmap)[1] <- "bc")
>
>
> Any help is appreciated! Thank you!
>

messages.author: cb81c117ced80308
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Changing population type
parts:
Hi Karl,

My population is a BC1F8 - the genotypes are  AA:AB:BB. It should be 3 AA:1 BB but its not a perfect system. Although most markers are segregating 3:1.  

There was an original cross made between P1 and P2 to create the F1, then the F1 was crossed back to P1 to create the BC1 (backcross1 generation). The BC1 was selfed to the F8 generation (basically it's a backcross followed by a RIL).

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Changing population type
parts:
At this point, it would be best to just treat this as RIL, using convert2riself() or convert2risib()

It would assume 1:1 segregation, but if you have reasonably complete marker genotypes, it shouldn't make much difference.

karl
